solutions.check: 28 entries verified against the grid (lengths, crossings, linked-clue mapping)

clue.text: America's leader needs second-rate party guys from which shit originates

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for a noun

indicators.note: the leader of a word is whatever stands at its front, so only its opening letter is kept

explanation.surface: A political jibe: the USA's president relies on second-rate party cronies who are the source of all the crap.
explanation.walkthrough: The political satire hides a plain anatomical definition: the belly houses the bowels.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly contains the intestines, where faeces are formed before leaving the body.

clue.text: Briefly place old Tory leader: "not hot – big nuisance"

indicators.note: said briefly, a word is cut down to its short abbreviated form
'not' asks for the letter standing for hot to be taken away

blocks.note: PL is the short form of place, as in street names
William Hague led the Conservatives from 1997 to 2001
H for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A quote about a former Conservative leader, dismissed as a big nuisance who is past it.
explanation.walkthrough: William Hague led the Conservatives against Tony Blair; 'not hot' is the signal to strip H, as on a tap, from his name.
explanation.definitionFit: A plague is used loosely of any persistent, widespread annoyance or pest.

clue.text: A minister casually dropping one in the morning: that's not abnormal

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so a letter is removed
done casually, things are thrown together in no particular order

explanation.surface: A government minister is caught carelessly dropping something early in the day, and everyone shrugs that this is normal.
explanation.walkthrough: Only one of the two Is in MINISTER is removed before the letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Something mainstream is conventional and ordinary, the opposite of unusual or deviant.

clue.text: Spin working, which gets you randy?

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun

blocks.note: a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A question about whether political spin, done well, is somehow arousing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Randy' is British slang for sexually eager.
explanation.definitionFit: A turn-on is anything that sexually excites or arouses someone.

clue.text: (& 23dn.) Lose ground, lose erection, lose love – end!

indicators.note: to lose something is to be without it, so a letter goes

blocks.note: to lose an erection, as the word before it says, is to droop
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O
the end of something is its rear, the part furthest from the front

explanation.surface: A grim list of an ageing man's losses: ground, potency, romance, and finally life itself.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'lose' is part of the definition; the second sits inside a phrase meaning DROOP; the third removes one O.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop back is to fall behind others in a race, ceding position.

clue.text: Hauled in, processed, not given the Caesar treatment

indicators.note: processed material has been worked over and changed in form

explanation.surface: A suspect is arrested and booked without any of the ceremony an emperor would get.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'Hail Caesar', the salute given to a Roman emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar was greeted with cries of 'Hail', so someone denied that salute goes ungreeted.

clue.text: Well, rest disturbed by the ultimate in Jimmy Riddle

indicators.note: something disturbed has been moved out of its settled order
the ultimate is the last, so only the final letter is kept

blocks.note: 'My!' and 'Well!' are both exclamations of surprise

explanation.surface: Someone's sleep is broken by the need for a Jimmy Riddle, rhyming slang for a piddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jimmy Riddle' reads as one phrase, but Jimmy supplies a letter and Riddle alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzle or enigma, something baffling and unexplained.

clue.text: Screw a party, Osborne initially going for a song

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter, here the one that is going away
something going is leaving, so it is removed

blocks.note: ball is slang for having sex

explanation.surface: Former Chancellor George Osborne writes off a whole political party for next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For a song' wants to mean cheaply; here 'for' is just a link and 'a song' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballad is a narrative poem or sentimental song, so it is one kind of song.

clue.text: Tender arse? Cry out: "stuffed by English knight!"

indicators.note: out can mean awry or wrong, so the letters are not in their proper order
something stuffed is filled up from inside, so a piece goes in the middle

blocks.note: an arse, as an insult, is a contemptible person, a cur
N is the knight in chess notation

explanation.surface: A sore backside prompts a yelp at being violated by an English knight of the realm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tender arse' reads as a sore bottom; Tender is the definition and arse is an insult meaning a worthless person.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is money that must be accepted in payment, which is to say currency.

clue.text: A coming of gold fuel on Motorway

blocks.note: M for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: Talk of a golden age of fuel arriving, perhaps a tanker on the motorway.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A coming' looks like an arrival but is meant in the sexual sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To come is slang for reaching sexual climax, so a coming is a climax.

clue.text: Member put in another bed (change of heart?)

blocks.note: a member is a body part, an organ
a gardener moves a plant to another bed

explanation.surface: A man's member ends up in someone else's bed, suggesting he has changed his affections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of heart' usually means changing one's mind; the question mark flags the literal sense of swapping a heart.
explanation.definitionFit: A heart transplant replaces the heart, a literal change of heart, and is one kind of transplanted organ.

clue.text: Magazine's to teach first hint of being an habitual wanker?

definitions.text: first hint of being an habitual wanker?

blocks.note: Private Eye is the magazine this puzzle appears in

explanation.surface: The magazine sets out to educate readers on spotting a chronic masturbator.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the old myth that masturbation makes you go blind, so tired eyes would be the first warning.
explanation.definitionFit: Strained, aching vision would be the earliest symptom on the road to the fabled blindness.

clue.text: Sun-originated sex alternative ensnaring city

indicators.note: to ensnare is to trap and hold, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: S as a short form of sex

explanation.surface: Something that came from the sun offers a substitute for sex, bathing a city in light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sun-originated' is the whole definition; 'sex alternative' splits into a one-letter abbreviation and the word offering a choice, and Los Angeles is the stock crossword city.
explanation.definitionFit: Solar means of or coming from the sun, as in solar energy.

clue.text: Potential film protection put on prince before shag

blocks.note: a screen gives shelter or protection
a lay is a sexual encounter

explanation.surface: A royal is urged to use a condom before sex, in case he ends up on film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Protection' and 'shag' set up a picture of a randy prince; protection is SCREEN, not a condom.
explanation.definitionFit: A screenplay is the written script from which a movie may later be made.

clue.text: Reckoning bloke's lost head over fox hunting event

indicators.note: losing the head means the opening letter is cut off
in a down-flipped sense, over means turned over and read the other way

blocks.note: HE'S, a bloke being a he
a hunt gathering is a meet

explanation.surface: A man has lost his temper over a fox hunt and is now facing a reckoning.
explanation.walkthrough: A meet is where a fox hunt's riders and hounds assemble before setting off.
explanation.definitionFit: Reckoning in the sense of judgment or estimation, as in 'in my esteem', the regard one holds.

clue.text: Despatching husband into drinking

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: sipping is a way of drinking

explanation.surface: A husband is being sent off because he has fallen into drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Despatching husband' reads as getting rid of him, but despatching alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Shipping goods is sending or dispatching them to a destination.

clue.text: In tatters, Trident advance

indicators.note: in tells you to look inside the following words for a run of letters

blocks.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Britain's Trident nuclear deterrent is in tatters, yet presses on.
explanation.walkthrough: Trident is the UK's submarine-based nuclear missile system; 'In tatters' looks like the anagram signal but 'In' alone does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: A stride is a long step forward, and progress made, as in making great strides.

clue.text: Showy walking band with "PM's lost lead"

definitions.note: a phrase describing the action, standing for a verb

indicators.note: having lost its lead, the word is missing its first letter

blocks.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn across the body
Theresa May, the Prime Minister when this was set

explanation.surface: A marching band strutting about with a banner reading that the Prime Minister has lost her lead in the polls.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was the British Prime Minister at the time.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk in an ostentatious, swaggering or flirtatious way.

clue.text: I say rogue Trump has lost millions – unethical

indicators.note: what has been lost is no longer there, so a letter is removed
a rogue thing behaves wildly and out of line, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: 'Cor!' is a British exclamation like 'I say!'

explanation.surface: An exclamation that the maverick Donald Trump has lost a fortune through crooked dealing.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove M from TRUMP, then rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Corrupt and unethical both describe dishonest conduct in breach of moral standards.

clue.text: Practised by May & co: "To awful misery, drained of energy"

definitions.note: a phrase describing a creed, standing for a noun

indicators.note: something drained has had its contents emptied, so a letter goes
awful suggests a mess, so the letters lose their order

explanation.surface: A satirical slogan for Theresa May's government: leading the country to dreadful misery, utterly exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove E from MISERY and rearrange; May led the Conservatives, nicknamed the Tories.
explanation.definitionFit: Toryism is Conservative Party ideology, the politics of Theresa May and her colleagues.

clue.text: "Oui, about to assume power" (May's opener – dope!)

indicators.note: about can mean turned around or moved here and there, so the letters move
to assume something is to take it on board, so a letter is taken inside
an opener is what comes first, so only the initial letter counts

explanation.surface: A French yes as someone is set to take power, with an aside calling Theresa May's opening move idiotic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dope' looks like an insult for an idiot, but here it means a drug.
explanation.definitionFit: Dope is slang for narcotic drugs, of which this poppy extract is one.

clue.text: Outlaw dead awful peers associated with a party

indicators.note: awful suggests something badly made, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A call to abolish the dreadful House of Lords members who are tied to a political party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' looks like a verb, as in banning the peers, but it is the noun definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless criminal or bandit, especially in the Wild West.

clue.text: Maybe cabbie changes political allegiance? Bollocks!

indicators.note: switching sides politically means moving from right to left, so one letter swaps for another

blocks.note: a cab driver is an example of a driver
L for left, replacing R for right

explanation.surface: A taxi driver suddenly switching parties draws a scornful 'rubbish!'
explanation.walkthrough: The R at the end of DRIVER, right, becomes L, left.
explanation.definitionFit: Bollocks is British slang for nonsense, and drivel means silly, worthless talk.

clue.text: Corbyn's principal affair (abandoning female) rattled the continent

indicators.note: the principal part is the chief or first, so the opening letter is taken
to abandon is to leave behind, so one letter is dropped
something rattled is shaken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A scandal about Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn's main romance, minus the woman, shakes all of Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The continent' in British usage often means mainland Europe; here it is a different continent.
explanation.definitionFit: Africa is one of the seven continents, the second largest by area.

clue.text: Turn appreciably dodgy – it's keeping Trump in power

indicators.note: something dodgy is unreliable and suspect, so the letters cannot be trusted to stay put

explanation.surface: A political organisation turns noticeably shady, and that is what keeps Donald Trump in office.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' looks like the anagram signal but it is part of the letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: Trump's US political organisation, the GOP, held Congress and backed him while he was President.

clue.text: see 5dn.
Autocratic president's measure to restrain opposition's chief Latin leftie

indicators.note: the chief part of something is its head, so the first letter is used
to restrain is to hold in, so one piece is kept inside another

blocks.note: a pint is a measure of liquid

explanation.surface: A dictator brings in a measure to silence the leader of the opposition, a left-wing Latin American.
explanation.walkthrough: Augusto Pinochet seized power in Chile in 1973, overthrowing the left-wing Allende; Che is the stock crossword revolutionary.
explanation.definitionFit: General Pinochet ruled Chile as a military dictator and styled himself its president.

clue.text: Group of political decision-makers said "we'd like a bung from you"

indicators.note: said means spoken, so what matters is how the words are pronounced

blocks.clueFragment: we'd like a bung from you
blocks.note: a bung is a cork, so the request is to stopper us

explanation.surface: A political committee is quoted openly asking for a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: A bung is British slang for a bribe, the surface sense; it is also a stopper, which gives the sound. In non-rhotic British speech the two words sound identical.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a meeting or bloc of party members who settle policy or candidates.
